fields.description:
## Context / Problem
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` is **799 LOC** against the locked
800-LOC hard cap (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), so the next agent to touch it — even to add a
comment — fails the CI module-size gate. Gerrit 1916 failed exactly that way on a sibling file.

## Approach
Split along the seam the module's own **import graph and call graph already draw**: the file holds
two disjoint function clusters that share no module-level import except `logging`.

**Cluster A — event-file materialisation (MOVES OUT).** `_RECONCILER_MARKER_APPLIER` plus the four
`_inbound_create_*` phase helpers (`apply_inbound_records.py:153-339`) and the four
`_inbound_update_write_edit_event` / `_write_status_event` / `_apply_labels` / `_apply_comments`
helpers (`:347-545`). Every one of them terminates in `inbound_translate._write_event_file`, and
they are the ONLY consumers of this module's entire module-level import block
(`projects_store`, `batch_dispatch._call_with_retry`, `_backend.TicketTransport`, `sys`, and all
13 names imported from `rebar_reconciler.inbound_translate` at `:31-44`).

**Cluster B — rebar-facade mutation (STAYS).** `_identity_provider_for` /
`_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity` (`:54-145`) and the closed link sub-graph
`_inbound_update_apply_links` → `_open_impossible_link_store` / `_open_peer_confirmation_store` /
`_skip_impossible_link` / `_note_impossible_link` / `_inbound_unlink_one` (`:548-799`). These write
through the public `rebar` facade (`rebar.ensure_identity_for`, `rebar.link`, `rebar.unlink`) and
the two sidecar stores, are all best-effort/fail-open with `logger` reporting, and write NO event
files. Cluster B keeps EXACTLY ONE name from the module-level block: `_extract_name`, used by
`_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity` at `apply_inbound_records.py:123`
(`display_name = _extract_name(assignee) or assignee.get("display") or ""`). So the retained
module-level imports are `logging` plus `from rebar_reconciler.inbound_translate import
_extract_name`; every OTHER name in the block (`sys`, `TYPE_CHECKING`/`Any`,
`_backend.TicketTransport`, `projects_store`, `batch_dispatch._call_with_retry`, and the other 12
`inbound_translate` names) has cluster A as its only consumer and moves with it. Cluster B's
remaining dependencies (`rebar`, `rebar.config`, `_backend_registry`, `_commands._seam`,
`_commands.unlink`, `impossible_links`, `peer_confirmations`) are already function-local imports.

Cluster A moves verbatim to a new sibling `apply_inbound_events.py`. Cluster B keeps the existing
file (and therefore its `logger` and its module identity), because two existing tests are bound to
that module OBJECT and would silently stop testing anything if the cluster moved:
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py:188`
monkeypatches `_open_peer_confirmation_store` on it, and
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_link_removal_2b16.py:643` captures logs on
`apply_records.logger.name`. Keeping cluster B in place preserves both without editing them.

The two cluster-A helpers that call `_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity` (`:214`, `:388`) import it
function-locally from `apply_inbound_records` — the idiom this module already uses for every
`rebar`/sibling dependency, and it preserves today's call-time (late) binding exactly, so an
existing monkeypatch of that name still takes effect. That direction keeps the import graph
acyclic: `apply_inbound_records` imports `apply_inbound_events` at module level for one documented
back-compat re-export (`_inbound_update_write_edit_event`, driven as
`air._inbound_update_write_edit_event` by
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_inbound_update_assignee_mint_5200.py:241,285`); the events module
never imports the records module at module level.

Why this approach: it is the only seam that (a) follows existing call-graph clusters rather than a
line count, (b) leaves both halves in the 200-500 LOC target band with 350+ lines of headroom each,
and (c) requires zero changes to any behavioural assertion.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_events.py` — NEW; receives cluster A verbatim.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` — keeps cluster B; drops the now-unused
  module-level imports; one documented re-export.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound.py` — repoint its phase-helper imports (`:34-47`)
  at the new module; `_inbound_update_apply_links` still comes from `apply_inbound_records`.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_inbound_apply_seam_split.py` — NEW seam regression test.
- `tests/unit/test_agents_serena_untyped_receiver.py` — one path anchor (see the docs bullet below).
- Path-keyed anchors that name the OLD location of moved lines and must be retargeted in this same
  change (each is a location anchor; no assertion is weakened):
  - `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py:62` — the single-`"jira"`-literal census
    is keyed to `apply_inbound_records.py`, but the literal lives in
    `validate_creation_channel("jira")` at `:222`, inside cluster A.
  - `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_live_oracles_discriminate_5200.py:217` — its `writers`
    tuple is keyed on file name (its docstring says it "must be retargeted whenever one moves");
    the `f"rebar-id:{local_id}"` literal it asserts is at `:292`, inside cluster A.
  - `tests/scripts/test_reconciler_core_seam_clean_heldout.py:54` — the config-ownership
    `_OWNED_FILES` registry; the new module is added so the split cannot shrink that gate's
    coverage. Its `_MARKER_BUDGET` / `_TOTAL_MARKER_CAP` are untouched: the new file carries zero
    `# read-via:` markers.
- `docs/code-navigation.md:61,80` and `docs/event-schema.md:261` — citations of moved symbols,
  retargeted to their true new home. Worked example for `code-navigation.md`: line 61 currently
  reads ``- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py:231` —`` and line 80
  ``- `apply_inbound_records.py:228```; BOTH cite `_inbound_create_writeback_jira`, a cluster-A
  symbol, and they are the doc's ONLY two occurrences of that file name. So an accurate retarget
  necessarily removes the string `apply_inbound_records.py` from the doc, which breaks
  `tests/unit/test_agents_serena_untyped_receiver.py:62`
  (`assert "apply_inbound_records.py" in doc`). Both lines are therefore retargeted to
  `apply_inbound_events.py` with refreshed line numbers, and that ONE assertion line in the test is
  retargeted to `assert "apply_inbound_events.py" in doc` — a fourth path anchor, not a weakened
  assertion: the test's intent (the doc evidences all three real `set_entity_property` call sites)
  is preserved exactly, and its two sibling assertions (`dispatch_one.py`, `binding_store.py`) are
  untouched. No stale or incorrect citation is left behind. ADRs are historical records and are
  left alone.

Assume no other consumer exists: verified with Serena `find_referencing_symbols` plus a plain `grep`
for every moved symbol name AS A STRING across `src`, `tests`, `scripts`, `docs`.

## Testing
New `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_inbound_apply_seam_split.py`, written RED before the
move (both assertions fail against today's single file):
- **Happy path / seam pinned:** `apply_inbound_records.py` contains no `_write_event_file(` call and
  `apply_inbound_events.py` contains no `rebar.link(` / `rebar.unlink(` / `ensure_identity_for(`
  call — the concern boundary cannot silently re-merge.
- **Edge / headroom:** both modules are >= 100 LOC and <= the near-cap band computed from the
  single-sourced limit in `.github/module-size-limit.txt` (`LIMIT - LIMIT // 10` = 720), so neither
  half lands back in the warning list. Reuses `tests/module_size_support` rather than restating the
  limit.
- **Import-surface preservation:** every one of the nine phase helpers plus
  `_RECONCILER_MARKER_APPLIER` still resolves through `rebar_reconciler.apply_inbound`, so the
  orchestrator's contract is unchanged.
Regression coverage is the existing suite, run unmodified:
`pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler tests/scripts -m "not integration and not external"`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Both halves are >= 100 and <= 720 LOC (real headroom, not one or two lines) — checked by the
      new seam test, which fails the build if either bound is crossed, and independently with
      `test $(wc -l < src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py) -le 720`.
- [ ] `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is byte-identical to `origin/main` — checked with
      `git diff --quiet origin/main -- .github/module-size-limit.txt` exiting 0.
- [ ] The new seam test fails on the pre-split tree and passes after — demonstrated by running it
      before the move (RED) and after (GREEN).
- [ ] No behavioural assertion is modified: the only test edits are the four path anchors and the
      one `_OWNED_FILES` registry addition named in Scope — verified by running
      `git diff --stat -- tests/` and confirming it lists exactly those files plus the new seam test,
      and by reading `git diff -- tests/` and confirming every changed line is a file path, a
      file-name tuple entry, or a registry entry.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler tests/scripts -m "not integration and not external"` passes.
- [ ] `make lint` (which includes `scripts/check_config_ownership.py` and the complexity ratchet
      `--check`) and `make typecheck` pass, with the ratchet reporting `new=0 increased=0`.
- [ ] Every moved symbol's references are updated — verified by BOTH Serena
      `find_referencing_symbols` and, for each moved name, `grep -rn "<name>" src tests scripts docs`
      returning no hit that still expects it in `apply_inbound_records.py`; the two searches and
      their results are recorded as a ticket comment.
